title: Neuroprotective Effects of Tenoxicam and Phenethyl Isothiocyanate in an Abeta(1)(-)(4)(2)-Induced Rat Model of Alzheimer's Disease: Modulation of NF-kappaB/NLRP3 Signaling and Redox Homeostasis.
authors: Kurmi, Shubham; Parab, Siddhi Bagwe; Godad, Angel; Waghmare, Prerna; Doshi, Gaurav
one_liner_zh: 该研究为阿尔茨海默病大鼠模型的药物神经保护作用研究，涉及NF-kappaB/NLRP3信号通路和分子对接，但核心对象非蛋白质-DNA互作，且无AI或物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder characterized by cognitive decline, neuroinflammation, oxidative stress, and amyloid pathology, yet effective disease-modifying therapies remain limited. This study asked whether combined targeting of inflammatory and oxidative stress pathways could offer enhanced neuroprotection in an Abeta1-42-induced rat model of AD. Tenoxicam, an oxicam-class non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug with COX-linked anti-inflammatory activity, and phenethyl isothiocyanate (PEITC), a natural compound known for antioxidant and Nrf2-activating properties, were selected on the basis of their complementary mechanisms; however, their combined potential in this model has not been sufficiently explored, providing the rationale for this hypothesis-driven investigation. Male Wistar rats were assigned to control, disease, standard, tenoxicam, PEITC, and combination treatment groups. Cognitive performance was evaluated using the Morris Water Maze, Y-maze, and Novel Object Recognition tests, while neuroinflammatory and oxidative stress markers, including NF-kappaB, NLRP3, IL-1beta, Nrf2, catalase, and malondialdehyde, were assessed alongside histopathological examination of hippocampal integrity and molecular docking against COX-2, NF-kappaB, and NLRP3. Abeta1-42 administration induced significant cognitive impairment, neuroinflammation, oxidative stress, and neuronal damage. Tenoxicam and PEITC improved behavioral performance, reduced inflammatory signaling, restored antioxidant defenses, and preserved hippocampal architecture, with the combination showing the most pronounced effects. These findings provide preclinical evidence that dual modulation of inflammatory and redox pathways may represent a promising multi-target approach for AD and support further evaluation of this combinatorial strategy.
abstract_zh: 阿尔茨海默病（Alzheimer's disease, AD）是一种进行性神经退行性疾病，其特征包括认知衰退、神经炎症、氧化应激和淀粉样蛋白病理，然而有效的疾病修饰疗法仍然有限。本研究探讨了联合靶向炎症和氧化应激通路是否能在Abeta1-42诱导的大鼠AD模型中提供增强的神经保护作用。替诺昔康（Tenoxicam）是一种氧昔康类非甾体抗炎药，具有COX相关的抗炎活性，而苯乙基异硫氰酸酯（phenethyl isothiocyanate, PEITC）是一种以抗氧化和Nrf2激活特性著称的天然化合物，两者基于其互补机制被选入研究；然而，它们在该模型中的联合潜力尚未得到充分探索，这为本假设驱动的研究提供了依据。雄性Wistar大鼠被分为对照组、疾病组、标准组、替诺昔康组、PEITC组和联合治疗组。认知功能通过Morris水迷宫、Y迷宫和新物体识别测试进行评估，同时检测神经炎症和氧化应激标志物，包括NF-kappaB、NLRP3、IL-1beta、Nrf2、过氧化氢酶和丙二醛，并结合海马完整性的组织病理学检查以及针对COX-2、NF-kappaB和NLRP3的分子对接分析。Abeta1-42给药诱导了显著的认知障碍、神经炎症、氧化应激和神经元损伤。替诺昔康和PEITC改善了行为表现，减少了炎症信号，恢复了抗氧化防御，并保护了海马结构，其中联合治疗的效果最为显著。这些发现提供了临床前证据，表明炎症和氧化还原通路的双重调节可能代表一种有前景的AD多靶点方法，并支持对该联合策略的进一步评估。
